en.q: A colour blind man marries a woman with normal sight who has no history of colour blindness in her family. What is the probability of their grandson being colour blind?
en.sol: Man XcY × normal woman XX → all sons XY (normal), all daughters XcX (carriers). A carrier daughter married to a normal man gives sons XcY or XY: probability of a colour-blind grandson (among her sons) = 0.5.
en.hint: The gene passes man → daughter (carrier) → grandson.

en.q: Thalassemia and sickle cell anaemia are caused due to a problem in globin molecule synthesis. Select the correct statement.

Both are due to a quantitative defect in globin chain synthesis
Thalassemia is due to less synthesis of globin molecules

en.q: What map unit (Centimorgan) is adopted in the construction of genetic maps?
o: A unit of distance between genes on chromosomes, representing 1% cross over.
A unit of distance between genes on chromosomes, representing 50% cross over.

en.q: The recombination frequency between the genes a & c is 5%, b & c is 15%, b & d is 9%, a & b is 20%, c & d is 24% and a & d is 29%. What will be the sequence of these genes on a linear chromosome?

en.q:
Which one of the following can be explained on the basis of Mendel's Law of Dominance?
A. Out of one pair of factors one is dominant and the other is recessive.
B. Alleles do not show any expression and both the characters appear as such in F2 generation.
C. Factors occur in pairs in normal diploid plants.
D. The discrete unit controlling a particular character is called factor.
E. The expression of only one of the parental characters is found in a monohybrid cross.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
o: A, C, D and E only
A, B, C, D and E
en.sol: The law of dominance: characters are controlled by discrete units called factors (D), factors occur in pairs (C), and in a dissimilar pair one is dominant and the other recessive (A). It explains why only one parental character is expressed in the F1 of a monohybrid cross (E). B describes the opposite. Answer: A, C, D and E.
en.hint: NCERT lists three points under the law of dominance.

en.q: With the help of given pedigree, find out the probability for the birth of a child having no disease and being a carrier (has the disease mutation in one allele of the gene) in F<sub>3</sub> generation.
en.sol:
In F1 a carrier mother and a normal father have an affected son, and only males are affected: the disease is X-linked recessive. In F2 a carrier female (XcX) marries her affected cousin (XcY; double line = mating between relatives).

XcX × XcY → XcXc (affected girl), XcX (carrier girl, no disease), XcY (affected boy), XY (normal boy), each 1/4. A child with no disease who carries the mutation = XcX = 1/4.
en.hint: Only carrier females can be disease-free and still carry the gene.

hi.q: दी गई वंशावली की सहायता से F<sub>3</sub> पीढ़ी में ऐसी संतान के जन्म की प्रायिकता ज्ञात कीजिए जो रोगमुक्त हो तथा वाहक हो (जीन के एक अलील में रोग उत्परिवर्तन हो)।
hi.sol:
F1 में वाहक माता और सामान्य पिता से प्रभावित पुत्र होता है, तथा केवल नर प्रभावित हैं: रोग X-सहलग्न अप्रभावी है। F2 में वाहक मादा (XcX) का विवाह उसके प्रभावित ममेरे/चचेरे भाई (XcY) से होता है (दोहरी रेखा = संबंधियों के बीच संगम)।

XcX × XcY → XcXc (प्रभावित पुत्री), XcX (वाहक पुत्री, रोगमुक्त), XcY (प्रभावित पुत्र), XY (सामान्य पुत्र), प्रत्येक 1/4। रोगमुक्त परंतु उत्परिवर्तन वाली संतान = XcX = 1/4।
hi.hint: केवल वाहक मादा ही रोगमुक्त होते हुए जीन रख सकती है।

en.q:
Which of the following statements are true with reference to the sex-determination in honeybees?
A. An offspring formed from the union of a sperm and an egg, develops as a female (queen or worker).
B. An unfertilized egg develops as a male by parthenogenesis.
C. A male has half the number of chromosomes than that of a female.
D. Males produce sperms by meiosis.
E. Honeybees have a haplodiploid sex determination system.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
o: A, B, C and E only
A, B, C and D only
B, C, D and E only
A, B, D and E only

• A ✓ fertilised egg → female (queen or worker).
  • B ✓ unfertilised egg → male (drone) by parthenogenesis.
  • C ✓ males are haploid (16), females diploid (32).
  • D ✗ males are haploid, so they make sperms by mitosis, not meiosis.
  • E ✓ this is the haplodiploid system.

A, B, C and E only.
en.hint: A haploid cell cannot undergo meiosis.

en.q: In pea, tall (T) is dominant over dwarf (t) and yellow seed (Y) over green (y), and the two genes assort independently. A TtYy plant is crossed with a Ttyy plant. What fraction of the offspring is expected to be tall with green seeds?
en.sol: Treat each gene separately (NCERT 4.3: in a dihybrid cross each character still segregates as in a monohybrid cross). Tt × Tt gives tall (T_) = 3/4, dwarf = 1/4. Yy × yy gives yellow = 1/2, green (yy) = 1/2. Tall and green = 3/4 × 1/2 = 3/8. (Dwarf and green would be 1/4 × 1/2 = 1/8.)
en.hint: Multiply the separate probabilities.

en.q: Which statement about sex determination in humans is correct?
o: The mother's ovum decides the sex of the child, since ova carry either X or Y
Males produce two kinds of sperm in equal numbers (X-bearing and Y-bearing), females produce only X-bearing ova, so the sperm decides the sex and each pregnancy has a 50 per cent chance of a girl
Of the 23 pairs of chromosomes, 22 pairs differ between males and females
A zygote with XY chromosomes develops into a female
en.sol: NCERT 4.6.1: human sex determination is of the XY type. Of 23 pairs, 22 pairs (autosomes) are the same in both sexes; females have XX, males XY. During spermatogenesis, 50 per cent of sperm carry X and 50 per cent carry Y; all ova carry X. Fertilisation by an X-sperm gives a female (XX), by a Y-sperm a male (XY). So the genetic makeup of the sperm determines the sex, and each pregnancy has a 50 per cent probability of either sex. Blaming women for the birth of daughters is a false notion.

hi.q: मानव में लिंग निर्धारण के बारे में कौन-सा कथन सही है?
o: शिशु का लिंग माता का अंडाणु तय करता है, क्योंकि अंडाणु में X या Y होता है

नर दो प्रकार के शुक्राणु बराबर संख्या में बनाते हैं (X युक्त तथा Y युक्त), मादा केवल X युक्त अंडाणु बनाती है, इसलिए शुक्राणु लिंग तय करता है और प्रत्येक गर्भावस्था में बालिका की प्रायिकता 50 प्रतिशत होती है
23 जोड़े क्रोमोसोम में से 22 जोड़े नर और मादा में भिन्न होते हैं
XY क्रोमोसोम वाला युग्मनज मादा में परिवर्धित होता है
hi.sol: NCERT 4.6.1: मानव का लिंग निर्धारण XY प्रकार का होता है। 23 जोड़े में से 22 जोड़े (अलिंग क्रोमोसोम) दोनों लिंगों में एक जैसे होते हैं; मादा में XX, नर में XY। शुक्रजनन में 50 प्रतिशत शुक्राणु X युक्त तथा 50 प्रतिशत Y युक्त होते हैं; सभी अंडाणु X युक्त होते हैं। X धारी शुक्राणु से निषेचन पर मादा (XX), Y धारी से नर (XY) बनता है। अतः शुक्राणु की आनुवंशिक संरचना ही शिशु के लिंग का निर्धारण करती है, और प्रत्येक गर्भावस्था में किसी भी लिंग की प्रायिकता 50 प्रतिशत रहती है। लड़की पैदा करने के लिए माता को दोष देना गलत धारणा है।

en.q: Which statement about genetic disorders in humans is correct?
o: DNA never changes, so disorders cannot be inherited
An occasional alteration in the genetic material is called mutation; genetic disorders are broadly grouped into Mendelian disorders and chromosomal disorders
Genetic disorders are studied in humans mainly by controlled crosses, as in pea
All genetic disorders are caused by the absence of a whole chromosome
en.sol: NCERT 4.8: the idea that disorders are inherited is old; after Mendel's work was rediscovered, inheritance in humans began to be analysed, mainly by pedigree analysis, since controlled crosses are not possible in humans. DNA is passed on without change, but changes occasionally occur; such an alteration in the genetic material is a mutation. Disorders linked to altered genes or chromosomes are broadly grouped into Mendelian disorders (mainly a single-gene alteration) and chromosomal disorders (absence, excess or abnormal arrangement of chromosomes).
en.hint: Two broad classes: gene-level and chromosome-level.
